content: 1. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the anthrax vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Additionally, immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 2. The combination of ustekinumab and equine antithymocyte globulin enhances immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 3. Similarly, ustekinumab and rabbit antithymocyte globulin also increase immunosuppressive effects and the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Ustekinumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Ustekinumab and axicabtagene ciloleucel mutually enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Ustekinumab and azathioprine both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Ustekinumab and basiliximab also increase immunosuppressive effects, leading to a higher risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live vaccines should not be administered during ustekinumab treatment, one year before starting treatment, or one year after discontinuation. 9. Ustekinumab and belatacept both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ustekinumab and brexucabtagene autoleucel mutually enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Ustekinumab and canakinumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Ustekinumab may alter the formation of CYP450 enzymes due to changes in cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor therapeutic effects closely. 13. Ustekinumab and cilta-cabtagene autoleucel mutually enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Ustekinumab and clindamycin require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 15. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating therapy. 16. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, and acellular pertussis vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating therapy. 17. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of diphtheria, tetanus toxoids, acellular pertussis, and inactivated poliovirus vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating therapy. 18. Ustekinumab and disopyramide require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 19. Ustekinumab and divalproex sodium require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 20. Ustekinumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while echinacea decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Efgartigimod alfa reduces ustekinumab's levels or effects through receptor binding competition. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness of medications that bind to the neonatal Fc receptor. Consider discontinuing efgartigimod if long-term use of such medications is essential. 22. Efgartigimod/hyaluronidase reduces ustekinumab's levels or effects through receptor binding competition. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness of medications that bind to the neonatal Fc receptor. Consider discontinuing efgartigimod if long-term use of such medications is essential. 23. Ustekinumab and ergotamine require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 24. Ustekinumab and etanercept both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Ustekinumab and ethosuximide require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 26. Ustekinumab and everolimus both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Ustekinumab and fentanyl require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 28. Ustekinumab increases the effects of fingolimod through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Ustekinumab and fosphenytoin require caution and close monitoring due to potential interactions affecting CYP450 enzyme formation. 30. Ustekinumab and glatiramer both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Ustekinumab and golimumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence is restored. 33. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 34. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 35. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 36. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection with live vaccines. 37. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Inactivated vaccines administered during ustekinumab treatment may not elicit a sufficient immune response to prevent disease. 38. Ustekinumab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Ustekinumab and hydroxyurea may increase the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ustekinumab and idecabtagene vicleucel mutually enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Ustekinumab and ifosfamide mutually enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ustekinumab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, adjuvanted) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating therapy. 44. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent, cell-cultured) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations before initiating therapy.
